a.text: Snow is falling on his head.
It turns into boiling water, into endless cries, into the weight of the dead.
Hands are not enough to sweep it away. It is wet, heavy, sinking...
Until it crushes those who are inside, those who are still living.

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: (Humming)

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Babushka, h-how are you feeling?

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: (Humming)

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: ...Tick, tock.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Tick, tock.

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: (Humming)

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: The clock, ticks, tocks.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: The clock, doesn't wait, for anyone.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: But we, shouldn't sing?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Let's... l-let's go.

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: No more survivors here.

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: I don't think I have the strength to stand. Are you there, Lidiya? I could use a hand—

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: Lidiya?

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: Over there.

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: Someone's coming.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Rankin...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: The fire's gone out.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Yes, it went out a while ago. Some survivors found us. We must do something.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Are you going to make Hawley kneel here forever? Even if he went mad and did all this, is it really necessary to punish him this way?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: The fire's gone out, and it's getting cold. He'll die.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Yes, he'll die. But...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Not yet.
Rankin looks toward the entrance to the village.
The fence that used to be there was designed to stop foraging tuskbeasts, not anyone determined enough to enter, whether their intentions were benevolent, or malicious.
Scattered figures begin to emerge from behind the remains of the fence.
They look this way hesitantly, then walk away timidly.
Rankin sounds almost like he is muttering to himself—

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I was wrong, Nikto.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I was wrong.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: In what way?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Hawley wasn't mad. He wasn't shouting for Vetochki's babushka, or to his dead son. He was shouting at me.

spans.text: Hawley wasn't mad. He wasn't shouting for Vetochki's
, or to his dead son. He was shouting at me.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: '...I have committed murder, not for food, nor for water, nor for abode.'

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: 'But for those who walk with me, for the salvation of their souls.'

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: I didn't hear anything. Even if he did say it, it's just the kind of prayer that Vetochki and her babushka pray all the time.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: It's not like they started worshipping the Yurodstvo and the Tsar yesterday.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Yurodstvo? Tsar? No, not distant or ethereal things like that. He was trying to save my soul, even after I made him kill his own son.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: But what is a soul, even? Who can prove that it exists? Is it more precious than mortal life? It's ridiculous... silly!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I shouldn't have forced him. But now, the worst has happened. If he did what he did before in order to fulfill my wishes, then it was for the same reason that he set this fire.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: No, it's nonsense, listen to me—

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: It might as well have been me who set this fire.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I must pay for my crimes.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Don't be a fool, Rankin!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I'll keep this brief.

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: What... what else do you have to say?

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: We gave you food and water.

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: Is THIS how you repay us?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: Are you here to chase us away, or to finish what you started?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I want you to witness the perpetrator face justice.

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: Ha... haha...

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: Hahahahaha...

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: Perpetrator? Justice? Will you kill all the arsonists, killers, and robbers in front of me?

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: No, you won't. Otherwise, you wouldn't be coming to talk to me while armed.

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: I'll pretend I didn't hear anything. Leave, unless you're trying to wipe us out.

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: Never come back again.
Rankin puts down his pickaxe and all other weapons, then raises both hands in the air.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Rankin!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Stay back, Nikto.

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: You still have your Arts...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Right here. The culprit is right here. You can do what you wish with him.

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I've put down my weapon. I won't use any Arts.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: You can do what you wish.

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: I see. You would shield the others with your own life.

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: I've never been good with numbers... but I can tell that's not a fair deal.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I'm right here. I won't fight back.

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: I don't want you! We don't want you! You weren't here when the fire started!

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: I want the one who set the fire, the one who robbed my home and burned it down—

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: I want the one who killed my wife!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Even if I was the reason for his violence?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: It was my arrogance that put the others in a desperate situation. It was I who forced him down the path of violence.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: You should kill me.

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Listen to me—

steps.name: Surviving Villager
steps.text: We want him. We don't want anyone else.
A small space has been cleared in the rubble to serve as an impromptu execution ground.
A crowd has gathered to watch. It is as though they cannot help themselves, like huddling around a fire in the winter night, yet fearful that its warmth might burn.

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: I still don't understand. Why did Hawley set the fire?

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: Why would he do this to a village that helped us?

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: He's mad.

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: He was never the same again after his son died.

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: But—maybe he didn't set the fire? Rankin wanted to satisfy the villagers, and Hawley happened to be sick.

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: The Hawley I knew would never do something like that...

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: I don't know, but I trust Rankin. Didn't you know? He even tried to trade his life for Hawley's.

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: Thankfully, the villagers wanted the real culprit, not a good person trying to take his place.

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: ...It hasn't started yet, but I can't watch...

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: I-I'll be over there. I need some rest.

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: Stop, Rankin's talking.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Pretty much everyone's here.

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: (Mutters) ...share...

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: (Mutters) Pain...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I have a few words to say before I execute this man. I'm not trying to defend him, or seek forgiveness from the victims.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Yes, he deserves to die.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: He betrayed kindness and trust. He placed all of us in danger. He harmed the innocent, in direct violation of our original intent, which was simply to survive.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Death may be inevitable on the path we chose, but it should never have happened this way.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Watch. Remember the lesson, and remember that the one about to take the life of this man is the one least qualified to do so.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I am executing him, on the wishes of the victims, and on my own decision.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: This will be the last decision I make as leader. No one should bear the burden of killing his own comrade. Therefore...

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: Repent...

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: Sin.
The snow has piled up on Hawley's shoulder. He kneels on the ground, as though he did not hear any of what Rankin said, and puts his hands together in front of his chest in a gesture of piety.
He looks up, and exposes his neck to the executioner.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Yes... I must repent my sins. I shall do the deed.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: (Whisper) Do vstrechi, Hawley.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Gah!

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Damn... I thought I could at least put this mirror together. Now it's gotten even more broken.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Talk about unlucky.

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: Can't we at least take Hawley's body, Rankin?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: What use do they have for a dead body? Do they want to leave it out in the wilds...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We're not in any position to negotiate.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Besides, all of you may come to the same end if you continue to follow me.

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Tired Miner
steps.text: Who do we follow, if not you? Now's not the time for jokes.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: It's not a joke. It's a decision.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: A decision that I already talked about.
Rankin turns around. The tired, unkempt crowd immediately gather around him, simply because he is here.
They look towards their leader, blankly waiting for the next instruction.

steps.name: Dazed Miner
steps.text: Do we keep going south, Rankin?

steps.name: Dazed Miner
steps.text: I don't have any strength left. I just wanted a roof over my head that could keep the snow away, but we don't even have that anymore, do we?

steps.name: Dazed Miner
steps.text: We'll die if we keep going...

steps.name: Dazed Miner
steps.text: We'll die if we stay.

steps.name: Sad Miner
steps.text: I couldn't find them, Rankin.

steps.name: Sad Miner
steps.text: Pavel and Bogina... I never found them, not even their bodies. I'm sorry.

steps.name: Sad Miner
steps.text: The villagers didn't want me anywhere near them, not even when I put down my pickaxe. They're afraid. You could see it on their faces from a mile away.

steps.name: Sad Miner
steps.text: I didn't want to threaten them. Let's go, Rankin.

steps.name: Sad Miner
steps.text: Take us away.
Rankin scans each face in the crowd, whether they spoke or not.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I'm sorry, friends.

steps.name: Sad Miner
steps.text: Rankin?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I can't decide your path going forward.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: As I said, it was not Hawley who should have been punished; it was me.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I was the one who drove him to madness and violence. It was my decisions that drove him to desperation.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Before this happened, I didn't even realize that not everyone was ready to look death in the eye.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: There's no longer any doubt. I don't have what it takes to be a leader. My last and best act as leader is to relinquish this position...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: And give you back the power of choice.
Silence.
Long silence.
No one answers. Hardly anyone even breathes, not so much a twitch on their faces.
All who hear the decision are silent, until a trembling voice emerges from the end of the procession.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: You're... abandoning... us?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: No, Vetochki.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Then, what? What you said... how do we, understand it?
The crowd parts for the one who asked the question.
Vetochki does not move forward. She stands where she is, her fists clenched so hard that her knuckles have turned white.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: You say, you won't lead, anymore! After we've come, so far?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Y-You're abandoning, all of us.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I'm not! I must do this, before things get worse for everyone.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: No more lives must be lost because of my foolish decisions. We didn't escape from the mines, that hellhole, for this.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: H-Hellhole? But it's, my home.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: The mines, mining district, is my... home.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: It was, many people's, homes.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Home? I thought you all wanted out, like me.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: It's because, of trust. We trust, you—Rankin.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: You... you didn't, know?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I thought you chose to leave because you've wanted to for a long time.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: You killed, the black bugs. You stood up, and said we, should leave, so... we left.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: You caught Hawley, killed him, and said, it was wrong, to leave. You said, it is, a choice.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I-I don't understand! What are we, to you?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Friends, family... it's complicated and hard to define. But it's exactly because you're important to me that—

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: This is, the home, of the villagers.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Maybe they can, rebuild the village. What about us? Where do... we go?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: You took us, so far. If you don't, lead anymore...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: How do, we go—go back?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Rankin, tell me...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: How do, we live?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Vetochki.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: No. The way you, call me. You're treating me, like a child. I-I'm not.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: You're not, talking back.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: You just proved what I had only guessed.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: All I've done up to this point was to force my ideas on you. You didn't understand my plan, you didn't understand the meaning behind my actions.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: You trusted me, not your own choices. What will you do when I'm not around to lead you?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I appreciate your trust, but this isn't right.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I'm going to tell you what's happening, and then you can make your choice.
Rankin once again scans each face before him, making sure that he has everyone's undivided attention.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Our ultimate goal is to reach the Kazimierzian border, and find the village of the Infected. In the process, though, this journey must become a reason for Ursus to recognize us.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: But it will put us in grave danger, because it challenges the very foundation of the Empire.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: People before us have tried and failed, leaving behind nothing but a symbol and a name, on this snowy, swampy tundra.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: What if I told you that following me might mean following in their footsteps? It's not something I would recommend for anyone who wants to live, anyone with a brain.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: But I never even gave Hawley a choice. That's why he's dead.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: He showed me that I must return the choice to you.
The crowd does not answer, but there is some faint commotion.
Slowly, the crowd begins to split. Some stand next to Rankin or behind him, others in front of him.

steps.name: Calm Miner
steps.text: When do we leave, Rankin?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Once everyone has made their choice.
More and more people move towards Rankin, their footsteps like the delayed ringing of the bell, announcing the end of a shift.
One, two, three... one miscount may mean one more soul lost to the mines.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Who doesn't, want to live?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Why do we, have to choose?
Vetochki can feel them growing more and more distant.
She subconsciously takes a step forward, trying to hold on to something, but someone grabs her and stops her in her tracks.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: —Vetochki.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: S-Serafina?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Y-You're going too? Where were you? I-I don't know, how to...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Th-They're all leaving! Leaving us to, go die!

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: It's alright, it's alright. I was just bandaging up Nikto, he cut himself on some broken mirror shards—

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: It's not important. I heard the last part of your exchange. You want to live. There's nothing wrong with that. You don't have to make yourself walk a path that you don't agree with, and I'm not going with them.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Y-You won't? You're not, leaving?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Yes, me and my team will continue to assist the wounded. Nikto is not leaving either, is he?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: ...Nikto?
The split crowd continues to move. Raidian could not see Nikto, so she begins scanning for a specific electrical signal with her Arts. It does not take her long.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: He's in the rear. He won't leave—

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: I'm sorry, Gospozha Serafina.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Nikto—

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: I'm sorry, Vetochki.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: I can't go back. You know that I came from Grypherburg. The mines were never my home.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Besides, it's not a sure thing that we'll die. Maybe things won't get so bad with me keeping an eye on the man.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: We must make opportunity with our own hands, after all, right?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: No. No, no, no!

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Why... why?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Why must, it be, like this?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Why must we... always...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: ...part?

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: Go home, Vetochki. Don't catch a cold.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: Go to bed, and mom and dad will be back when you wake up again.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: Be a good girl who doesn't cry or complain, make your babushka happy... and you'll find a piece of chocolate on your pillow when you wake up!

spans.text: Be a good girl who doesn't cry or complain, make your
happy... and you'll find a piece of chocolate on your pillow when you wake up!

steps.name: Indistinct Voice
steps.text: ...Strike...

steps.name: Indistinct Voice
steps.text: Rights... no... response...

steps.name: Indistinct Voice
steps.text: ...Execution...

steps.name: Strange Voice
steps.text: 'Mama.'

steps.name: Strange Voice
steps.text: 'Papa.'

steps.name: Strange Voice
steps.text: 'Ditya.'

steps.name: Strange Voice
steps.text: ...'Babushka?'

steps.name: 'Babushka'
steps.text: (Hums)

steps.name: Anxious Voice
steps.text: One word! Just one word!

steps.name: Anxious Voice
steps.text: One word, and my soul will be healed!

steps.name: 'Babushka'
steps.text: (Hums)

steps.name: Anxious Voice
steps.text: —I beg forgiveness... for the sin...

steps.name: Anxious Voice
steps.text: Of killing your child...

steps.name: 'Babushka'
steps.text: 'I shall...'

a.text: 'I shall meditate and share in your pain.'
'For you, for him. May we all repent our sins from the bottom of our hearts.'
'Thy blessings walk, on earth as it is in heaven.'

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: ...Babushka?

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: (Hums)

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: ...Babushka...

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: (Hums)

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Babushka... is someone, outside?

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: No one stops, no one waits.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: They're... gone.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: They cry, kiss your hand, say they didn't, want to be apart... but they're gone.

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: Everyone has their own path.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Must this be? But, why...

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: You know the reason, suffering soul.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Rankin... never taught me... how to, read that watch.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Second hand, clock...? I can hear, the bell.

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: As always.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Babushka... why is your hand so cold?

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: The fire is hot.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I'm cold... and it hurts...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: But it's not... because of, fire.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I don't understand...

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: It's alright. Most people live their entire lives in obliviousness.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Until... they die?

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: Yes, until they die.

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: (Hums)

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Babushka... what are you, singing about?

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: Love.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: But I... hurt?

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: Because you love.

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: Love makes people hurt, makes them persevere, makes them docile.

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: Love makes people strong, makes them wealthy, makes them noble.

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: You love, and therefore you hurt. I love you, and therefore I share in your pain.
Vetochki says no more. She closes her eyes and curls up tightly, but no longer dares touch the hand that caresses her cheek as usual.
She had heard these words before, back when she did not need to find support for them amongst broken pieces. Now, though, she is no longer sure.
How can one be more wealthy and noble than kings and nobles if one lives in obliviousness?
How can one be stronger than the stick of authority if one is powerless?
The campfire is very near. It should have brought warmth, but Vetochki feels cold in her limbs, her innards, every part of her body—
Passing through the cold, withered hand.

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: 'I shall meditate and share in your pain.'

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: 'May we all...'

steps.name: Nadia
steps.text: '...repent our sins from the bottom of our hearts.'
The voice is simply a repetition, an echo.
The echo points towards... doom.
